# The appointments Gawain made — and who is keeping them

Take Gawain's stories in sequence. They are not episodes; they are appointments — and the modern trades are keeping them.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Gawain
- **Pantheon:** Celtic
- **Domain of influence:** Knight, Sun Hero
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Society & Spirit · Commerce & Governance · Culture & Entertainment
- **Strongest seat:** History, Archives & Records
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 171 of 546

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### History, Archives & Records — through *The Knight Who Finished the Quest*

The oldest Arthurian tale in Welsh names him in its great muster at Arthur's court: Gwalchmei mab Gwyar — Gwalchmai son of Gwyar — 'because he never returned home without achieving the quest he had gone to seek; he was the best of walkers and the best of riders; he was nephew to Arthur, the son of his sister, and his first cousin. ' In a catalogue of hundreds of warriors, giants, and wonders, that is the whole of his entry, and it is the whole of his character: the Welsh tradition remembers him not for a single exploit but for completion itself — the errand that always comes home.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The full transmission chain: Gwalchmai → Walganus → Gauvain → Gawain, traceable text by text.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Legal, Justice & Compliance — through *One of the Three Well-Endowed Men*

The Welsh Triads — the medieval memory-system that files the Island of Britain's heroes in threes — name Gwalchmai son of Gwyar among the Three Well-Endowed Men of the Island of Britain, beside Llacheu son of Arthur and Rhiwallawn Broom-Hair (Triad 4).  Rachel Bromwich's edition of the Triads is also the standard witness for his name: Gwalchmai, gwalch 'hawk' + Mai 'May', the 'hawk of May' — a name that stands in Welsh before any French romance ever sang of Gauvain.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The Green Knight's test — the contract kept to the letter, the fault confessed to the syllable.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Sports, Fitness & Competition — through *The Nephew of the King*

Geoffrey of Monmouth's Historia (c.  1136) made him Latin and sent him across Europe: Walganus, son of Loth of Lodonesia and Arthur's sister Anna, given as a boy to the service of Pope Sulpicius in Rome, recalled to Britain to be knighted, and made the steel edge of Arthur's Roman campaign — the knight who cuts through the emperor's host and slays the nephew of Lucius.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *He never returned home without achieving the quest — the courteous athlete of every cycle.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Gawain's dossier runs from a Welsh triad to a fourteenth-century masterpiece: in every century someone is testing him, and the test is always the same — not whether he can fight, but whether he will keep faith.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity’s documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. ## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in history, archives & records, legal, justice & compliance, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/gawain/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
